$why: Moved out of run-agent-orchestration.sh on 2026-08-16. The brownfield addendum every QA
These gates were designed for a freshly-scaffolded application. Pointed at 850+ existing
files and a three-line change, only TWO of six mentioned the code the run had changed
(2026-07-26): sast spent its budget on 70 pre-existing dependency CVEs, review-ranger
returned a 211-byte pass without naming the diff, perf-sentinel was handed browser E2E
context for a backend string comparison, and fuzz-weaver returned nothing at all.
Two corrections: judge THIS CHANGE, and be allowed to say the change is not your business.
Silence is indistinguishable from failure and a fabricated pass is worse than both, so
not_applicable is a first-class verdict with a required reason.
The file list arrived as a shell default-expansion whose fallback sentence was itself
prompt text. The caller supplies the whole value now, fallback included: prompt wording
hidden inside ${VAR:-...} is wording nobody reviews.
description: The brownfield scope addendum appended to every QA gate prompt.
body:
## BROWNFIELD — judge THIS CHANGE, not the codebase
This is an existing production repository. It contains problems that predate this
run and are none of this run's business. You are reviewing one small change to it.

Files this run produced or modified:
__FILES__

RULES:
1. Findings MUST be about the lines this run changed. A pre-existing issue in an
   untouched file, or on an untouched line of a touched file, is NOT a finding
   here — reporting it blocks a correct change over somebody else's problem.
2. If __GATE__ has nothing meaningful to say about a change of this kind, return
   verdict "not_applicable" with a one-line reason. That is a valid, useful
   answer. Do NOT invent a finding to look thorough, and do NOT return "pass" to
   mean "I could not evaluate this".
3. Prefer fewer, real findings over broad coverage.
